intent: Continue the agility direction that has raised slalom progress every iteration since iteration 3, with two small steps from the iteration 6 design: mass to the 0.40 kg minimum and wheel_track to 0.11 m. Keep the sensor array, wheel radius, and body envelope unchanged so the oval and s-bend completions and the Integrator's controller carry over. Expect more slalom completions while holding oval and s-bend.
learning: Iteration 6 confirmed that body narrowing and lower mass moved slalom finishes from 0 to 14 of 20, so yaw response is the limit on alternating bends. Next iteration, check: (a) whether slalom finish rate rises above 0.7 with the 0.40 kg mass and 0.11 m track, which would confirm further agility helps; (b) whether steering_oscillation on the slalom rises above 0.30, which would mean the gain has outrun the damping and the Integrator needs more kd, or that wheel_track should go back to 0.115 m; (c) whether oval and s-bend completion rates hold at 20/20 and 18/20 or better; (d) whether slalom max_error falls below 0.06 on the seeds that now go off_track. Ask the Integrator whether kd or ki needs retuning after the mass and track change.
rationale:
Iteration 6 is the best design so far (score 883.9). Oval and s-bend both finish 20/20, and slalom now finishes 14/20 (mean progress 0.94, up from 0.53). Every agility change since iteration 3 (lower mass, shorter body, narrower track, narrower body) has raised slalom progress without hurting the oval or s-bend. The remaining slalom failures are off_track endings (6/20), which points to turn response on alternating bends, not sensing or speed: line_loss_events are about 1 per run, and the slalom finish time of about 2.0 s leaves speed margin.

The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at the 0.06 m floor at body_width 0.08 m, so there is no further body-width lever. Body_length is already at its 0.10 m minimum. The remaining yaw-inertia levers are mass (0.42 kg, minimum 0.40) and wheel_track (0.115 m).

Changes in this proposal, applied to the iteration 6 design: (1) mass 0.42 to 0.40 kg, the allowed minimum, which lowers yaw inertia by about 5 percent; (2) wheel_track 0.115 to 0.11 m, which adds turn authority per unit of wheel differential, as narrowing the track did in iterations 4 and 5. Sensor positions, sensor_size, wheel_radius, and body dimensions are unchanged, so the Integrator's controller carries over. I am keeping the step small because the iteration 4 to 5 and 5 to 6 steps showed that oscillation stays near 0.30 on the slalom, and a large track cut risks more jitter.

Expected result: slalom finishes rise from 14/20 toward 16 or more, slalom max_error stays below 0.06 on most seeds, and oval and s-bend completions hold at 20/20 and 18/20 or better. Risk: steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 with more turn authority, which would need more kd from the Integrator.
